name: Abell 3322 (Hubble)
blurb: Abell 3322, a massive galaxy cluster, seen by Hubble.
label: smacsj051024519-hubble
story: A cosmic leviathan of galaxies that shines brightly in X-rays, with its brightest members lined up as if the cluster were still taking shape. Clusters like this act as gravitational telescopes, magnifying more distant objects behind them.

claims.text: Abell 3322 is a massive galaxy cluster imaged by Hubble; central galaxy 2MASX J05101744-4519179 at RA 5 10 17.69, Dec -45 19 24.12 (matches the pointing)
It is highly luminous at X-ray wavelengths, a 'cosmic leviathan'
Its brightest cluster galaxies are aligned, suggesting the cluster is observed in formation
Clusters like this act as gravitational telescopes through lensing
SMACSJ0510.2-4519 is a target of Ebeling's snapshot survey of extreme clusters (program 16670)
